data.gender_notes: Galla is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word γαλλός (gallos), which means 'of Gauls' or 'milk'. In Greek mythology, Galla was a nymph who presided over milk and nursing. This name has a rich spiritual connotation, symbolizing nourishment, comfort, and protection. The name Galla carries the meaning “River of milk” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Galla usually hope their child will grow to embody river of milk and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: "Galla" is not a commonly used Christian name, but its origins can be traced back to the ancient Greeks, specifically to the Gauls, a Celtic people who inhabited Greece during ancient times. The name Galla carries with it a connection to the Gallic culture, emphasizing strength, resilience, and deep-rooted traditions.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian spirituality, the name Galla holds great significance, drawing from its Greek roots where it symbolizes the provision of nourishment and comfort. The name evokes images of the Virgin Mary, who is often referred to as the source of all spiritual nourishment. Mary's role as the Mother of God means she is the spiritual mother, providing unending comfort and protection to all her children. The name Galla, therefore, can serve as a reminder of the divine providence and inexhaustible love of God.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Galla may be derived from the Celtic word "gal," meaning "foreigner" or "stranger." In a Christian context, this name could symbolize a deep connection to the outsider, the unconventional, or the stranger in our midst, reminding us of God's love and acceptance of all people, regardless of background or status. Alternatively, it could represent the inner stranger within each of us, the part that is still seeking and growing, and the journey towards finding our true selves in God.

historical_references.reference: Galla Placidia was the eldest daughter of Emperor Theodosius I and his wife Flavia Galla. She ruled as Regent of the Western Roman Empire from 421 to 433 CE and was a strong supporter of Christianity throughout her reign.

historical_references.reference: Saint Gall, a Benedictine monk in the 6th century CE, was born in Gaul (France) and is the namesake of the Abbey of Saint Gall, which was one of the major centers of learning and culture in Europe during the Middle Ages.
